[h1] Build 0191.1 Development Branch [/h1]
[list]
[*] Added extra checks to prevent cards from sticking on their target if the drag operation interrupts midways ie. mouse issue.
[*] Slightly reduced Concealment Values & halved Concealment values in Actions with Echo as in this case the values stack before enemy gets to attack.
[/list

notes.title: Patch Notes - Build 0190
notes.content:
[h1] Build 0190 [/h1]

This is a fairly large update (to download :P) as it both lays down the foundation for the upcoming sandbox/exploration mode and replaces all the old placeholder stage graphics. 

It also removes completely the 'Paths', as it was a source of confusion, and replaces them with fairly large Dungeons, Bandit Camps & Caves to explore.

I tried not to break your existing save games, so any Path nodes in your current game will act as a dungeon, bandit camp or cave node instead, and if you were in a  stage with only paths and no boss, a boss will now appear at the end of the stage. [b]Still I would recommend to start a new run.[/b]

[h1]Misc changes & improvements[/h1]

[list]
[*] Renamed 'Enemy Gallery' to 'Enemies Compendium'
[*] Renamed 'Card Collection' to 'Player's Handbook'
[*] Added a button in 'Player's Handbook' that will display the stats,disciplines,proficiency & resistances of the chosen Class (or Race) in the side panel.
[*] Replaced all the placeholder stage graphics with new stage graphics
[*] Events will no longer offer exploration opportunities. 
[*] Removed Paths & Replaced them with Dungeon, Bandit Camp & Cave nodes (depending the environment)
[*] Dungeons, Bandit Camps & Caves act like Caves were but now add a quite large amount of new nodes to explore.
[*] You can drag & reorder enemies. Which you can think of it as changing their relative position in the battlefield to your character. Reordering enemies changes:
[list]
[*] The order in which enemies act & decides which enemy will receive the retribution damage first.
[*] The targets of your multicast actions (that for example target the first 2 enemies)
[*] The target of your right click shortcut (targets the first enemy)
[/list]
[*] Minor UI changes to accommodate the changes listed above.
[/list]

If you encounter any issues or bugs with the new update let me know.

I'll dedicate the couple next builds to smooth things out and refine any rough edges. (For instance finding a Town in the middle of an infernal cavern is something that might happen, and won't be making much sense.) Once everything works out properly both in flavor and function, I will start working on the Sandbox mode.

[h1]Build 0190.1[/h1]
[list]
[*] Combat log will clear only each time you advance a node. It will stay intact for the whole duration of the encounter unless the text limit is reached. (You can still clear it manually at any time.)
[*] Chain effect was destroying the original target instead of the chain target on lethal damage.
[*] Restricted the environments towns can appear
[/list]

[h1]Build 0190.2[/h1]
[list]
[*]Restrictions as to where towns & exploration nodes could appear where too strict making their appearance way too rare & random.
[*] Towns will (once more) appear (in most game modes) at Stages 3,5,7 and have a 50% chance to appear in (most stages) after Stage 9.
[*] Exploration nodes will appear (in most game modes) at Stages: 3 to 7 and have a 75% chance to appear in (most stages) after Stage 9.
[*] Neither Towns nor Exploration nodes will appear inside other exploration nodes & stages that use interior graphics (like the infernal cave in Stage 8)
[*] Added additional checks and improved error handling in the Wildshape code
[*] Whenever a Lycanthrope uses the Wildshape effect to assume their Hybrid form, and as long the transformation is last, their Avatar Card will now change to reflect that. The character sheet avatar will remain unchanged.
[/list]

notes.title: Patch Notes - Build 0189
notes.content:
[h1] Build 0189 [/h1]

[h1] New Action Effects [/h1]
[list]
[*] MulticastAll:1
[list]
[*] Action will Clone itself, then target & affect every enemy separately. (Replicate, Echo & Multicast effects aren't copied.)
[*] Exact wording is: Multicast (All). & detailed description: "This Action Targets & Affects (separately) all Enemies."
[/list]
[*] Multicast:x
[list]
[*] Action will Clone itself, then target & affect the x first enemies separately. (Replicate, Echo & Multicast effects aren't copied.)
[*] Exact wording is: Multicast (x). & detailed description: "This Action Targets & Affects (separately) the first x Enemies."
[/list]

[b] Notes for Modders: [/b]

[list]
[*] Multicast Actions have effect only if the resolved target is an enemy. Players will receive any beneficial/harmful effects automatically each time the Multicast action clones. i.e [Multicast:3, Damage:3, Defend:3] can damage up to 3 targets for 3+ Damage & the player will receive up to +9 Defend (Adjust beneficial effects accordingly).
[*] Multicast Cloned Actions don't cost any additional AP to the player. (Adjust the initial cost accordingly.)
[*] Multicast Actions will gain an additional +1 XP each time they clone. i.e 3 XP for 2 Targets etc leveling up much faster, but the Multicast effect itself won't increase when a card levels up.
[/list]
[/list]

[h1] New Actions [/h1]

Added around 54 new Actions & Equipment across all the Classes, Races & Loot database. Replaced several Card Artworks and adjusted several Cards effects (In particular all actions with retribution have now slightly different effects. If your mods override Actions from the Core Set, you may want to update their entries to match the updated Core Set ;)

[h1] Retribution Nerf [/h1]

[list]
[*] Retribution value will drop each time you use it to deal damage to enemy. 
[*] If Retribution is higher than the amount necessary to kill an enemy, the remainder amount is used on the next enemy or debuffs normally if no other enemies exist.
[*] Adjusted Actions with Retribution to account for the effect nerf. Either Retribution is higher or the Action costs less AP.
[*] Effect text changed to: "Retribution x" & detailed description to: "Distribute up to x Intense Damage to each Enemy attacking you this Turn."
[*] Summon Retribution & Defend benefits remain unchanged till we evaluate the impact of this change in game difficulty.
[/list]	


[h1] Bugfixes [/h1]

[list]
[*] Weaken Effect was applying an incorrect counter count & was resetting in some cases.
[*] Custom Card Artworks weren't showing on the side details panel.
[*] ModManager wasn't properly purging all deactivated Databases.
[*] Summons weren't leveling up instantly once they had accumulated the necessary XP.
[/list]

notes.title: Patch Notes - Build 0188
notes.content:
[h1] Build 0188[/h1]

[h1] New Perks [/h1]

Added 36 new Perks, using the properties introduced in the previous build. Between the new perks and some of the older ones each Race & Class got plenty of new options:
[list]
[*] Additional Race Perks:  +2 Human, +6 Vampire, +6 Lycanthrope, +8 Demon
[*] Additional Class Perks: +6 Animist, +6 Necromancer, +6 Exorcist, +6 Witch, +6 Hunter, +6 Shadow, +6 Mystic, +6 Mercenary.
[/list]

(Also added a reminder in the Character Sheet that Perks Lists are scrollable since I really dislike scrollbars.)

Perhaps the most interesting new addition, are the Perks granting new Disciplines. 

Each Class now has 2 Perks that allows them to gain access to another Class Card Set. For instance at Level 8 the Mercenary can spend 375xp and gain access to the Shadow's Cards or to Hunter's Cards, or eventually spend 750 xp and get access to both.

This won't make your Mercenary a Shadow, as you'll have to slowly grind or buy all the Shadow cards you like, neither will give you Mastery as Shadow. But will give much more choices and options and spice up your Endless run. You can even add your new Shadow Cards as Skills (by spending tokens).

[h1] Modmanager Improvements [/h1]

You no longer need to restart the entire game after activating, deactivating, installing or uninstalling mods. The formerly 'Restart' button in ModManager is renamed to 'Restart ModManager' for better clarity on what it does. Restarting ModManager button, will take a few seconds for reasonable mod setups. It will purge all cached mod data from memory, and reload them. So always click this button after you install,uninstall,activate or deactivate any mods.

[h1] Misc Changes & QoL Improvements [/h1]

[list]
[*] Added setting to adjust the speed of Enemy Attack Cards (1.2s,1.5s,2s,2.5s,3s & 3.5s) default value is 1.2s
[*] Changed the Enemy Attack Card 'animations' behaviour to delay slightly to start, giving more time to read the card

[*] Changed the description of Circle of Light & Darkness to Consecrate x & Desecrate x.

Effects now read: 

[b]Consecrate x[/b]: Area emmits an Aura of Light for x Turns. Undead & Demons lose (ActionTier + EvolveCardBonus) HP. Everyone else restores (ActionTier + EvolveCardBonus) HP.

[b]Desecrate x:[/b] Area emmits an Aura of Darkness for x Turns. Undead & Demons restore (ActionTier + EvolveCardBonus) HP. Everyone else loses (ActionTier + EvolveCardBonus) + HP.

Notice that the Negative Aura Effects cause [b]loss of life[/b] (thus they cannot be resisted and are not subject to resistances or weaknesses)

Additionally Aura of Darkness & Light now cancel/dispel each other, regardless their tier. A relevant message will display in the log.

[*] If the Fatigue system is active in your Game Mode, after each Action a Concentration x/y reminder will now appear. Fatigue will kick in, after your Concentration drops to 0.

For example seeing in the core Ironman mode "Concentration 0/6", means that the 7th Action you'll use will cause +1 Fatigue. As a reminder Fatigue can be disabled completely or become more punishing by editing the corresponding Game Mode text files or by creating your own custom Game Modes. ([url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1703719938]See the Modding Guide[/url])

[*] Hovering over an Echo indicator will now highlight its target (if its target exists. Echo actions with no target dispel at the beginning of EoT)
[/list]

[h1] Bugfixes [/h1]
[list]
[*] Fixed an issue with Enemy AI Response triggering even though the enemy was just destroyed a few seconds ago. Same issue could cause under certain cases exception errors. [i] (but let me know if an enemy proves too stubborn to accept death, and cause any additional issues)[/i]
[*] Fatigue Threshold was incorrectly increasing when Echo Actions were echoing.
[/list]

notes.title: Patch Notes - Build 0187
notes.content:
[h1] Build 0187 [/h1]

[h1] Modding Additions & Enhancements[/h1]

This build adds many new modding additions and enhancements, including fully customizable game modes, new perk keywords, new action keywords, SFX modding improvements and some quality of life improvements & bugfixes.

[h1]Disciplines[/h1]

All Classes & Races can now 'inherit' Cards from any other Class or Race. The Cards an Archetype can find & use are now declared in the 'Disciplines' section for the archetype. In practice this means that Custom Class & Race Archetypes can now inherit Cards from other Classes & Races.

For example let's say you wanted to make a Succubus race, but want it to be able to use the core Demon Cards. Now you can by using in the Succubus Archetype: 

"Disciplines":[ 
"Succubus", 
"Demon" 
] 

[h1] New Perk Properties to use in your Custom Perks[/h1]

[list]
[*] AddDiscipline:[Discipline] & RemoveDiscipline:[Discipline], can give or remove disciplines from the Player. 

ie. AddDiscipline:Mystic, RemoveDiscipline:Mercenary will give the Player the Mystic Discipline but remove the Mercenary Discipline. The player will be able to find only Mystic cards in Merchants & Grimoires but not Mercenary cards, even if before they could.

Disciplines determine the cards you can find, so losing or adding disciplines don't change your class or your skills

[*]  ModifyEffect[CardEffect]:x, can permanently alters how any numerical card effect is treated by the player. 

i.e ModifyEffectDefend:-1, means that from now on, in all cards with Defend value, the Defend value for the player is -1 point less.

i.e ModifyEffectConcealment:20, All cards that provide x% Concealement, from now on provide 20% more concealment etc.
[/list]

[h1] Card Collection fully supports custom races & classes [/h1]

Card Collection Filters are scrollable and are now populated dynamically by all defined races & class (Custom Class & Race Cardsets will now appear in the Card Gallery). Any Cards with the same type as class/race or of discipline belonging to class & race will appear in the collection

i.e If you have a custom class Blademaster, with Disciplines(Blademaster & Mercenary), both the Blademaster & Mercenary cards will get listed when view class cards

[h1] Game Modes are fully Moddable [/h1]

[list]
[*] In addition to editing existing game modes, you can now use the Mods folder to create any number of new Game Modes you wish.

Put the [GameMode].json files in Mods/[Your Mod]/GameModes & declare them under 
>> GameModes in your ModLoaderUser.conf

[*] Your mod can also change Casual, Normal, Ironman & Endless modes, leaving the core files untouched. Your mod's modes have priority and override any core files they change.

[*] The Game Modes selector is scrollable & any loaded Modes will be displayed there giving you the choice to play any of them. You are also free to remove any core modes you don't use by editing the original ModLoader.conf.
[/list]

[h1] Mod Manager can now Activate or Deactivate Mods [/h1] 

You can now deactivate mods without Uninstalling them. Just toggle on/off the Checkmark under the mod name. (It's always a good idea to restart the game after Activating, Deactivating, Removing & Adding Mods.)

[h1] SFX Modding Additions & Improvements [/h1]

[list]
[*] Enemy Attack, Impact, Death SFX & AI Response sounds can be changed by modders.

While declaring the Enemies you can use AttackSFX:[Soundfile], ImpactSFX:[Soundfile] && DeathSFX:[Soundfile].

Sound filename doesn't have to be a number. 

i.e AttackSFX:ZombieMoan, ImpactSFX:BludgeoningImpact, DeathSFX:ZombieDeathCry 

[*] AttackSFX will play on attack start, ImpactSFX on attack impact & DeathSFX on enemy death. These Audio Files should also be located in ../Mods/[My Modname]/Audio/SFX

[*] Currently core Enemies play only the Impact SFX and by default is their Damage Type i.e Bludgeoning. You can override all default Impacts of a type ie. all Bludgeoning impacts by providing a Bludgeoning.wav file.

[*] You can override all special actions Effects i.e. the Gallop AI response, by providing a Gallop.wav file etc.

[*] Card Activation Effect can now be set with the new and more versatile ActivationSFX:[Soundfile] which doesn't have to be a number & it can also use internal resources.

i.e ActivationSFX:Poison will look for a file called Poison.wav (or mp3, or ogg) and play it each time the card activates.

[*] Clicking an enemy on the gallery will also play its AttackSFX file (which by default isn't set)

[*] Clicking a Card in Card Collection will display a larger artwork + the uncut version of the Card text & play its SFX impact sound, whether its internal or custom.
[/list]

[h1] New Action Effects [/h1]

[list]
[*] Festering x: If the Target is Bleeding, Festering Wound deals x Intense Damage to them.
[*] Resist[DamageType] x: Give the Caster resistance to a specific DamageType x, till the end of turn.

i.e. ResistSlashing:2, ResistPiercing:-2 will give +2 Slashing Resistance & -2 Piercing Resistance till the beginning of your next turn (This effect de-buffs after all enemies attack).
[/list]

[h1] Misc Changes & Improvements [/h1]

[list]
[*]Rearranged Race & Class selectors to allocate space for more races & classes before it's necessary to scroll
[*] Removed the ink button from Enemy Gallery. Simply clicking on the card will display the Enemy info.
[*]Whenever using an Action causes the Player or an Ally to gain or lose life due to its effects a relevant message displays in the log.
[*]Towns will now always appear in Stage 3, 6 & 8 [Final Stages for Casual, Normal & Ironman] (instead of 3,5,7)
[*]After Stage 8+ Towns have a 50% chance to appear in a Stage or not
[*]Added a few new Actions in Vampire, Demon, Shadow, Exorcist & Animist
[/list]

[h1] Bugfixes [/h1]

[list]
[*] Card Evolution & XP were incorrectly saving only for Cards in Deck & for Cards in Hand.
[/list]

notes.title: Patch Notes - Build 0186
notes.content:
[h1] Build 0186 [/h1]

[h1] QoL Improvements, New Features & Additions [/h1]
[list]
[*]Clicking on Enemies (you have defeated) in the Enemy Gallery (or in the icon above their card) will now display their resistances, immunities & weaknesses. Displayed Stats are from the initial (lowest) level instance of that enemy. (Note though that, in higher levels Enemies can develop new or just higher resistances. So think of the Gallery as the equivalent of a PnP monster manual.)
[*]Hovering over the 'Action in Effect' indicators (Lingering Echo Actions) will now display the text of the original card as a quick reminder.
[*]Decluttered the initial Log entry to only display the Difficulty Settings. (A Tutorial hint will only appear if the player has collected less than 5 tokens.)
[*]The Button to show/hide the Town will only appear in Town node, as it's useless everywhere else.
[*]Added a Quick help button in the Log to complement the tutorial and explain the basic game controls & shortcuts.
[*]When clicking any of the Help buttons, the Log will automatically scroll to the top. In every other case, as entries are added in the Log it will automatically scroll to the bottom (similar to a chatbox).
[*]Added a semitransparent background behind the enemy name to improve readability.
[*]Consumables can no longer convert into skills, through the 'S' button. (Not that it would cause any issue, but it would have been inconvenient to keep adding them back after they get consumed.)
[/list]

(As promised, I also updated the modding guide to include information about Game Modes, Custom SFX & Custom Perks.)

notes.title: Patch Notes - Build 0185
notes.content:
[h1]Build 0185[/h1]

[h1]QoL Improvements, New Features & Additions[/h1]
[list]
[*]You can now not only increase, but also decrease any Attribute down to 6. Either to fine-tune them or to get more points to spend in other attributes.
[*] You can spend 5 tokens to add a non-Skill Action card to your Skills list. Once added to your Skills list the action will behave exactly like a skill for the duration of the run. Meaning you can freely add or remove it from your deck at any time. To convert a non-Skill action to a Skill, go to your Deck (D hotkey) and click on the 'S'-labeled button which will now appear in all non-Skill Actions in your Deck. 
[*] Deck Max size increased from 30 to 60 Cards (20 triplets, 60 singles or whatever).
[*] Skills, Equipment & Deck areas are now scrollable.
[*]Deck count will now instantly refresh as you add & remove cards from the Skills or Deck UI.
[*]Do note, that any Deck change or Perk addition is saved along with your Progress. For that matter, your game progress is now saved automatically after proceeding to the next node (instead of only entrances & campsites)
[*]Added 9 new (medium to high level) Enemies (3x Ooze, 3x Serpentfolk, 3x Golems)
[*]New AI Responses: Hybrid Form & Animal Ally.
[/list]

[h1] Card SFX are Moddable[/h1]
[list]
[*]Modders can change the sound effect that plays when using an Action Card
[*]Audio files must be placed in Content/Mods/[Your Modname]/Audio/SFX
[*] WAV, MP3 & OGG files are all supported.
[*]If a UserAudio flag is found in Card Declaration, the Modmanager will attempt to load the SFX file named as the card or as the numerical value of the flag. i.e Assuming you want custom SFX for 'Brutal Strike', add UserAudio:1 to the card declaration, then either a filename called Brutal Strike.wav or 1.wav in the SFX folder (in case you want to use the audio file more than once.)
[/list]

notes.title: Patch Notes - Build 0184
notes.content:
[h1] Build 0184 [/h1]

Build 0184 brings an additional way to further customize your character and make them even stronger: [b]Perks.[/b]

[h1] Passive Perk System [/h1]
[list]
[*]Added 10 Perks in each Race & 10 Perks in each Class (Common perks unlock at different levels depending the class & race strengths)
[*]Perks can be bought with XP & give your Character passive bonuses for the duration of the run. XP spend on Perks are permanently lost delaying your Level Up, some time significantly. So it's up to you whether and when to use them.
[*]Common Perks between your Race & Class can only be picked once. But in such cases the perk unlocks earlier in either your race or class, so you can pick it up from wherever it unlocks first.
[/list]

It goes without saying, that if you used to find the game easy before, it will be way easier after investing your hard-earned XP in some perks. I will be mitigating that soon, with an AI abilities expansion. So perhaps in the meantime you can test it out in the endless mode ;)

[h1] Modding the Perk System[/h1]
[list]
[*]Modders can both modify and add custom Perks in Core/Custom Races & Classes
[*]Perks are defined in .tdb files placed in ../Content/Perks
[*]Currently Perks can Increase/Reduce Attributes, HP, AP, Handsize, Proficiencies & Resistances, but more Perk effects will be introduced in the coming builds.
[*]Any Perk .tdb declared under >> Perks in a ModLoader will be automatically parsed and added to the Perks Database.
[*]Perks appear in the Perks section of Character Sheet based on the Archetype's PerkTree section.
[*]I haven't forgot that I haven't updated the Modding Guide yet with the Game Modes and now with the Perk additions. Will do so in the coming days. ;)
[/list]

[h1] Misc Changes & Bugfixes [/h1]
[list]
[*] Added an extra 0.5s delay between each Enemy Attack to give more time in the attack SFX to complete before starting the next one.
[*] Having lost your unique companion could cause an exception error in save points (like camps or dungeon entries) leading to progress loss and various game errors.
[/list]

notes.title: Patch Notes - Build 0183
notes.content:
[h1] Build 0183[/h1]

[h1] Hotkeys [/h1]
[list]
[*]'Esc' key toggles (hides/shows) Main menu. When toggling it, the Main Menu state will stay intact (for example if you leave the Card Gallery open, opening the Main Menu will get you right back there).
[*]'Space' key triggers [End Turn/Continue]. You can also Close (and Skip) Events & Loot Nodes by pressing the Space key [End Turn/Continue].
[*]'C' key toggles (hides/shows) the Character Sheet in [Skills (Default)] view
[*]'S' key opens/switches Character Sheet in [Skills] view
[*]'P' key opens/switches Character Sheet in [Perks] view
[*]'E' key opens/switches Character Sheet in [Equipment] view
[*]'D' key opens/switches Character Sheet in [Deck] view
[*] 'X' key will hide all Popups (Character Sheet, Events, Loot & Town). (If you close an Event or Loot window with this key, it's gone for good and you can't undo this action.)
[/list]

[h1] Misc Changes & Improvements [/h1]
[list]
[*]You can now Pay 2 HP & discard any unwanted card from your hand by dropping it to the Backpack next to your Deck. (The Backpack will highlight when you are over the right spot).
[*]When targeting an Enemy immune to a certain effect, or if the effect will fail 100% because the action/caster is much lower level than the enemy,
the message will now read: "[Effect] fails: [Target] is either Immune, or Action Level is too low to affect them". When the effect is resisted due to the 25% chance, the message will still read: "[Target] resists [Effect]".
[*]When breaking a negative effect because you dealt damage i.e to a Stunned enemy, a more clear message will display in the log to warn you: i.e for Stun Effect: "Beware! This attack removed 1 Immobilized counters from [Target]".
[*]Applying Settings will now also hide them.
[/list]

[h1]Bugfixes[/h1]
[list]
[*]Character Sheet opens above the Echo Effects indicator
[/list]

notes.title: Patch Notes - Build 0182
notes.content:
[h1]Build 0182[/h1]

I am still in the process of implementing the passive Perk system as well as laying the groundwork for an enhanced enemy AI. So that enemies will be able to use cards like the Player. But meanwhile in the morning I stumbled into an ER gameplay video by one of our community members. 

Seeing the game from a 3rd person's perspective helped me a lot to notice a couple of places and wordings that could use improvements and make their functionality somewhat clearer. And on that note, I would really love to see more gameplay videos from the community, hear and see your frustrations and improve whatever I can improve. 

Of course you can always drop by the forum and let me know too. Even if I can't do something right away I'll consider it for a future build.

[h1] Misc Changes [/h1]
[list]
[*]When a card reaches the highest upgrade the preview text will change to Tier x [Level x (Max)], to indicate that the maximum upgrade of the card reached.
[*]Detailed Explanation & Card Level/XP (in Card Preview) now display in a gray color, to easily skip reading them, once you are more familiar with the various effects.
[*]Echo x wording changed for more clarity on how the effect works: "As long as Action's Target is alive, Action Effects last/repeat for x Turns. While an Action is Echoing, all its other Instances lose Echo."
[*]Primal Actions will now display their Type. ie. Primal Slashing, Primal Piercing etc.
[*]Actions that count as Primal, will now display their type. i.e Primal Slashing. This is important as Actions that count as Primal also amplify their Primal Element type. This will also now display in the Detailed Explanation window.
[/list]

[h1]Bugfixes & Card Corrections[/h1]
[list]
[*]In certain cases of Echoing Damage Bonus, Card Text wouldn't update but the card preview would still display the correct damage
[*]Frozen, Immobilized or Bewitched enemies should no longer perform any special actions or trigger special AI responses
[*]Custom Card Artwork wasn't appearing in Deck & Skilltrees
[*]Custom Card Artwork wasn't appearing if the custom Card was a Summon (in the Ally) or if it had Echo (in the Echo indicator)
[*]Omega,Beta & Call the Pack Lycanthrope Actions now count as Primal Slashing.
[*]Supernatural Durability action now counts as Primal Earth.
[*]Animist Animate Tree now counts as Primal Bludgeoning.
[/list]

notes.title: Patch Notes - Build 0181
notes.content:
[h1]Build 0181[/h1]

[h1] All Game Mode properties (that matter) are now Moddable [/h1]
[list]
[*]ModLoaders upgraded to load any GameMode.json files declared under >> GameModes & and placed in Content/GameModes/ (But currently only the Core Game Modes including Casual, Normal, Ironman & Endless can be played & modified)
[*] Game Mode Aspects that can be altered by editing the appropriate game mode files include:
[list] 
[*]Number of enemies that appear in Normal & Elite Encounters [MinEncounterNormalNum,MaxEncounterNormalNum,MinEncounterEliteNum,MaxEncounterEliteNum]
[*]How higher can be the Elite Enemy Level in comparison to that of Normal Enemies [EliteLevelDifference]
[*]The XP Gain Multiplier [XPGainMultiplier]
[*]Bonus Starting Hit Points [InitialHPBonus]
[*]Whether this game mode is Endless or Not [Endless]
[*]If the game mode is not Endless after how many Stages the Gaunlet will be completed [StagesToCompleteTheRun]
[*]How many Tokens & Mastery will be awarded if the Gaunlet is complete [RunCompletionRewardTokens, RunCompletionRewardMastery]
[*]If Permadeath is forced or not [PermaDeath]
[*]If Reincarnation takes a toll (value multiplied by stages cleared) [ReincarnationToll]
[*]Whether Fatigue system is on or off [Fatigue]
[*]If the Fatigue system is on how much is the threshold before it kicks in [FatigueThreshold]
[/list]
[/list]

[h1]Balance Changes[/h1]

Now that everyone is free to set their own fatigue settings and change their game mode settings as they please, I decided to increase the fatigue threshold a bit, and adjust the stage lengths to what I think should be the vanilla difficulties.

[list]
[*]Casual Mode ends after 3 Stages & awards on Completion +5 (Bonus) Tokens & Mastery. Fatigue will incur at 10+ Actions.
[*]Normal Mode ends after 6 Stages & awards on Completion +10 (Bonus) Tokens & Mastery. Fatigue will incur at 8+ Actions.
[*]Ironman Mode ends after 8 Stages & awards on Completion +15 (Bonus) Tokens & Mastery. Fatigue will incur at 6+ Actions.
[/list]

[i]There is also an endless mode, but currently is very experimental and a work in progress. For now I just needed it to establish the modding framework regarding Game Modes. If anyone wants to try it out, let me know of your thoughts on the difficulty and boss scaling after stage 8, everything before that should be similar to Ironman except the XP Gain, Starting HP bonus & Fatigue threshold.[/i]

[h1] Bugfixes [/h1]
[list]
[*]Ending Turn without using any Cards would draw bonus cards in some cases
[*]Wildshape code could lead into an exception error in some rare cases
[/list]

notes.title: Patch Notes - Build 0180
notes.content:
[h1]Build 0180[/h1]

There are 2 big changes you will notice in this build. 

One, is that the enemies will no longer move towards your direction to attack you, but instead conjure a card and literally throw it at you. Additionally, each time an Enemy is about to use a special ability, a card will also appear briefly to notify you. The floating damage no longer appears in the PC portrait, as I found it distracting to properly observe the attack & status enemy cards.

The second important change is the Fatigue system.

[h1] Fatigue [/h1]

Each time you use a card after a certain threshold (defined by the game difficulty) you gain +1 Fatigue. Then for each fatigue counter the AP cost of your Actions increase by +1.

[list]
[*]Casual: You can use 8 Actions before incurring fatigue penalty.
[*]Normal: You can use 6 Actions before incurring fatigue penalty.
[*]Ironman: You can use 4 Actions before incurring fatigue penalty.
[/list]

Let's say for example that you play in Normal. You can use 6 Actions without incurring a Fatigue penalty. The 7th will increase your Fatigue by +1, so the 8th Action will cost +1 AP and will further increase your Fatigue by another +1, so the 9th Action will cost +2 AP etc. At the End of Turn any fatigue penalty you have incurred is lost.

I doubt that this change will affect you much in Casual & Normal, but hopefully will give you an increased challenge in Ironman. You don't have to remember any of this, as cards AP cost will update accordingly. This is a big change and the values used before you incur the penalty are experimental. Let me know of your thoughts in the forum.

There is also a new Action Effect "Fatigue:x" for modders to use while crafting Actions. This effect increases or reduces the Caster's Fatigue by x.

[h1] Other Balance Changes [/h1]
[list]
[*]Various Actions adjusted based on the Community feedback
[*]Slightly Increased the Boss level (for the purpose of resisting negative effects)
[*]Each time per turn you use Amplify to boost an Action's damage without the Amplify effect, will now reduce your Amplify bonus by 25%, (down to 2.) This is tracked separately for each element, i.e. Amplify bonus in "Slashing Damage" will be reduced when you deal Slashing Damage.
[/list]

[h1]Bugfixes[/h1]
[list]
[*]Card descriptions wouldn't refresh immediately after transitioning to a new area and Empower had just de-buffed.
[*]Card Count in deck wouldn't refresh right away as Grimoire or Purchased cards were added in it.
[*]Area Graphics should now cycle properly in higher Nodes
[*]Enemies could move and hide behind each other while performing their attack animation. This should no longer be an issue, as enemies are no longer moving. (But let me know if it's still happening when they die though.)
[/list]

notes.title: Patch Notes - Build 0179
notes.content:
[h1] Build 0179 [/h1]

As of this build, the only reported issue that remains in my list to fix is a more sophisticated save state for the Consumable items (with more than 1 uses). This isn't really a high priority item though and is planned to arrive shortly after Sandbox mode is finished. [i]The issue is that all consumables of same type are tracked collectively, and their counter resets once one is destroyed from your deck. End result, is that you do use them as many times as you are supposed to, but a) the counters are confusing and b) also reset once you reload the game. Therefore is necessary to have a separate save-state reflecting the exact status of all consumables in deck, but it can certainly wait.[/i] 

Unless I forgot something important, or something urgent arises that needs fixing in the coming days, I'll skip publishing a couple of builds in order to start working on some new features, that will take significant planning and code base changes.

First in order will be the passive perks and afterwards a sandbox exploration mode that will pave the road for the story mode.

So if you have any ideas on passive perks feel free to drop by the forum, and let me know. 

The way passive perks will work, is that you'll be able to exchange earned XP to unlock passive bonuses for your character. These will be racial and class based ie. Vampires & Lycanthropes might have a perk giving them Slashing Resistance, or increased Speed (AP cost reduction). Mercenaries may have perks improving their training with various weaponry etc. Of course spending XP on perks will delay Leveling up, so it's a choice you have to consciously make.

On a different note, in this build I heavily adjusted all the Actions in the game, to reflect the collective feedback regarding balance so far. And while I doubt this will make the game more difficult for those struggling in late stages, it might make it much easier for everyone. So looking forward to hear your thoughts on that.

[h1] QoL Improvements [/h1]
[list]
[*]Added a Game mode & difficulty indicator under the player's level in Character Sheet.
[/list]

[h1] Balance Changes [/h1]
[list]
[*]I went through all the Actions and adjusted/lowered where necessary their AP costs or increased their damage, based on the overall community feedback regarding balance so far.
[/list]

[h1] Bugfixes [/h1]
[list]
[*]Amplify & Imbue Effects in Echo Actions were first cast & then immediately debuffed when there wasn't enemies present during the end of turn.
[*]Wildshape incorrectly allowed to use non primal Actions after the Echo Fixes in 0178 build
[*]Added an additional check to prevent fast-clicking causing the End of Turn logic, to trigger more than once.
[*]Only bonus cards (from Echo) are now drawn during the start of End of Turn. All new Cards and Equipment are now drawn & activate after all enemies have acted.
[*]Empower AI response had a multiplier of range (2 to 3) instead of 2.
[/list]

[h1]Build 0179.1[/h1]
[list]
[*]Primal Damage wasn't adding up to normal Damage if a card had both properties (i.e the 'Cat Claw' weapon)
[*]Echo Actions Draws count as Bonus Draws and are subtracted from the normal Drawing phase
[*]Echo Copies was of Level 0, even if the originating Action was of a higher level
[/list]

[h1]Build 0179.2[/h1]
[list]
[*]Fixed an issue with weapon cards not appearing after shapeshift end
[/list]

[h1]Build 0179.3[/h1]
[list]
[*]Focus & Invoke effects count more accurately the cards in players hand (as cards are drawn and discarded asynchronously count might have been inaccurate in some cases)
[*]A message will display to notify you how many cards you draw & if the hand size limit reached
[*]A message will display to notify you when non-primal cards got discarded and how many while wildshaped
[*]Summons will now properly deal any additional damage to Vulnerable enemies
[/list]

notes.title: Patch Notes - Build 0177
notes.content:
[h1] Build 0177 [/h1]

I am aware that a better save state is needed for the Summons and Consumables, and I am working on a solution for it. This patch is focused mostly on balancing issues.

Many voiced the concern that the minimum Deck size of 6 is too small, and I agree. So the highlight of this patch, has been to adapt all classes & races to a new minimum Deck size of (12). There is also a major overhaul of the Exorcist class, several reported bugs fixed and a couple more suggested balance changes. 

There are still a few minor reported issues unresolved, but I am working on them, so keep the bug reports coming ;)

[h1] Balance Changes [/h1]
[list]
[*]Reduced the cost of most Exorcist Actions & in several cases boosted slightly their effects, [*]Adjusted Exorcist Skills
[*]Reduced the cost of several Witch & Mercenary Cards
[*]Increased Minimum Deck-size to 12
[*]Each Race got 6 additional Cards as skill cards
[*]Adjusted the Starting Cards of all Classes & Races
[*]Enemies with level higher than [Card Tier + Card Level + Your Level + Your Empower] are now immune to Kill effect
[*]Boss level (for the purpose of resisting negative effects) is no longer fixed but depend on their Stage [1.5 * D + 3] rounded down i.e D0 = 3, D1 = 4, D2 = 6 etc.
[/list]

[h1] Bugfixes [/h1]
[list]
[*]Character Sheet was displaying wrong values for Intellect & Willpower
[*]Attribute order in Character Creation matches the Attribute order in Character Sheet
[*]In character creation, when the last used character appearence had saved, clicking on outfit would switch to the 1st character appearance
[*]Consecrate Effect had the description of Desecrate Effect.
[*]Echo Summons were disappearing instantly or appearing without artworks
[*]Improved the Code handling Summoning & Unsummoning/Death of Allies
[/list]

notes.title: Patch Notes - Build 0176
notes.content:
[h1] Build 0176 [/h1]

Improvements, Balance changes and Bugfixes based on the community feedback.

[h1] Quality of Life Improvements[/h1]
[list]
[*] Added a field in card preview displaying its Tier, Level & XP
[/list]

[h1] Balance Changes [/h1]
[list]
[*] Each time per turn you use Empowered Actions without the Empower effect, will now reduce your Empower bonus by 25%, down to 2.
[*] To keep the ruleset clear & simple: Using Summon Actions also fall into this behavior (while in the previous Build casting summons would reduce your Empower bonus to 0.)
[*] 2x, x3 & x4 Damage modifiers are calculating individually for each enemy when a spell deals AoE damage.
[/list]

[h1] Bugfixes [/h1]
[list]
[*]Player wasn't drawing cards while in Hybrid form or Wildshaped
[*]Intense Damage wasn't receiving the Evolution or Empowerment bonuses
[*]Empower was applying twice in Self cards
[*]Added an extra mechanism to prevent dead summons to linger after the turn ends.
[*]Added extra measures to prevent exceptions & bugs caused by the card drawing algorithm
[*]Drawing mechanism should no longer freeze in cases where more cards were requested than the actual amount of cards left in the deck (in a single action).
[*]The moment the deck runs out of cards is reshuffled, and drawing resumes if possible.
[*]Drawing sequence will stop once the player has their entire deck in hand
[*]Area graphics would disappear if the player had reached node higher than 370
[*]Weaken could drop the Enemy power to 0, instead of the minimum value of 1
[/list]

I had more balance changes planned for this build, but some major bugs came up that needed to be addressed urgently. So stay tuned for more balance changes in the coming build after Easter. Looking forward to hear your thoughts about the Empower change in the forum.

notes.title: Patch Notes - Build 0175
notes.content:
[h1] Build 0175 [/h1]

Improvements, Balance changes and Bugfixes based on the community feedback.

[h1] Quality of Life Improvements[/h1]
[list]
[*]When choosing a race or class their Dominant Attributes combination is displayed marked in colors.
[*]Dominant attributes now also appear color coded in the Character Sheet. (These are the attributes that will increase during each level up, starting from the lowest to the highest etc.)
[/list]

[h1] Balance Changes [/h1]
[list]
[*] When attacking with a Summon an Immobilized, Frozen or Bewitched Target, it doesn't get counter-damage, but 1 relevant counter is removed from the enemy for every 3 damage dealt (above 3). i.e. 1 counter is removed if dealt 3-5 damage, 2 counters if dealt at 6-8 damage etc.
[*] When the player damages Immobilized, Frozen or Bewitched Target, 1 counter breaks for every 3 damage dealt (above 3). ie 1 counter if dealt 3-5 damage, 2 counters if dealt at 6-8 damage etc if the action doesn't have this effect. If it does the damage you dealt is treated as 3 points lower than the actual damage you dealt. ie. 1 stun counter is remove if the action has stun but you also dealt 6-8 damage, 2 counters are removed if dealt 9+ damage etc. (Each time a counter is removed from the enemy a relevant message will also appear in the combat log.)
[*] Enemies with level higher than [Card Tier + Card Level + Your Level + Your Empower] are now immune to certain card effects .i.e A level 4 Enemy can no longer be affected by a Level 1 Character casting a Tier 1 Stun spell. A relevant message will appear in the combat log.
[*] Amount of Encountered Enemies changed to further vary the 3 Difficulty Modes
[list]
[*]In Casual Mode: 1 to 3 Normal Enemies may appear in the same encounter or 2 to 3 in Elite Encounters
[*]In Normal Mode: 2 to 4 Normal Enemies may appear in the same encounter or 2 to 3 (+1 level higher) in Elite Encounters
[*]In Ironman Mode: 3 to 4 Normal Enemies may appear in the same encounter or 3 to 4 (+1 level higher) in Elite Encounters.
[/list]
[/list]

These balance changes should have a great impact on the game difficulty, compared to the previous build. So looking forward to hear your thoughts in the forum.

[h1] Bugfixes [/h1]
[list]
[*]Shadow Class was assigned the (wrong) Generic Dagger instead of their designated one.
[*]Echo spells were not echoing when using the Double-click method AND a summon was present
[*]Consumbles were used up each time an effect was forcing them to discard
[*]Increasing an Ability during Level Up was displaying wrong value in the Combat log when the Attribute was either Willpower or Charisma.
[/list]

notes.title: Patch Notes - Build 0172
notes.content:
[h1]Build 0172[/h1]

[h1] Modding Extensions & Built-in Mod Manager for Zipped Modpacks[/h1]
[list]
[*] All current Modding Capabilities can now apply to self-contained Mod folders. 
[*] Any Mod folder placed in Content/Mods will activate automatically ie. Content/Mods/[Your Mod Name] as long as all the proper files are in place.
[*] A Mod Folder can contain either a ModLoaderUser.conf file
[*] Or Actions & Encounter Databases
[*] Or PC Artworks (Ragdolls)
[*] Or Archetypes
[*] Or CustomArtworks
[*] Or all of the above

Properly structured zipped files will unpack to Content/Mods/[Your Mod Name], and display as [Your Mod Name] in the Installed Mods section. Their contents will become immediately available after you click on the Restart button located in the Manage Mods UI.
[/list]

[h1]Bugfixes[/h1]
Added extra checks to prevent cards from sticking on the player's avatar [This bug is very rare and i was unable to reproduce it consistently, I think it's fixed now. Let me know if it reappears after you install this build!]

notes.title: Patch Notes - Build 0171
notes.content:
[h1]Build 0171[/h1]

[h1]Initial Difficulty Controls & Permadeath Rules[/h1]

You can now choose between 3 Difficulty Settings:

[b]Casual[/b]
If your character dies you can choose to retain your savefile and return back to main menu, or reincarnate and receive your bonus Tokens & Mastery.

Special Rules: Your character starts with +5 Hit Point but gains 20% XP less than Normal.

[b]Normal [/b]
If your character dies you can choose to retain your savefile and return back to main menu, or reincarnate and receive your bonus Tokens & Mastery.
 If you choose to retain your savefile you'll lose 1 Token per stage cleared (-0 at 1st Stage, -1 at 2nd, -2 at 3rd etc)

[b]Ironman[/b]
Death is final. The moment you die your savefile is gone, and you can only reincarnate and receive your bonus Tokens & Mastery. 

Special Rules: Your character gains 20% XP more than Normal.

[b]Developer's notes:[/b] These are some initial settings to establish the basic code framework handling difficulties. By no means are final, but they should provide a slightly different experience while keeping things somewhat fair. Eventually these difficulties will be changing much more aspects of the actual gameplay difficulty, but i still need your feedback and thoughts regarding balance before starting to messing things up more. Existing saves (for compatibility purposes) will be treated as if you chose the "Casual" Difficulty.

notes.title: Erannorth Reborn Gameplay 102
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34785691/502081d99341c0dea95594dc020bc70fdee1b92e.jpg[/img]

When creating a single-player Deck-building game it's inevitable to draw comparisons with the most widely known game of the genre's present (StS).

Respect. Not only it has revitalized and popularized the genre, but has been the source of inspiration of an entire generation of amazing Deck-building games. In fact its quite surprising, that we don't have yet a Spirelike, or Spirelite tag here on Steam. That would certainly describe many games, Erannorth Reborn included.

Now while Erannorth Reborn, does share a lot with StS gameplay. I would go with the tag Spirelite, to describe ER rather than Spirelike, if it existed. 

Ok. For one because StS wasn't a direct inspiration of mine as a game but as an idea, and because I was inspired mainly by the many of its modern offsprings (and predecessors of ancient times [i]namely the 1998 Duels of the Planeswalkers by MicroProse[/i]). And each of these past and present games, left me with different unique mark.

I did play StS briefly though and I will try to describe some notable Gameplay differences; so you won't be disappointed when you won't find your favorite mechanic or realize that some important things you came to love in that game are handled way differently here. 

Since my experience is mostly of similar games, I will collectively refer to them as Spirelikes, so don't be upset if something I describe isn't a feature of StS but of one of its offsprings, and feel free to comment below and correct me.

[h1]Similarities with StS and other Spirelikes[/h1]

You fight enemies with cards in procedurally generated environments, you acquire new cards in the process to build a better deck, which is the only way to advance further and further. Once you die, it's over, but thankfully you unlocked new stuff in the process that will help you do better in your next run.

[h1]15 Differences with StS or other Spirelikes[/h1]

1) There is a large subset of cards you can unlock, [b]that you can then add or remove them freely from your Deck any time[/b]. These represents the combined Skills of your Class & Race. In fact your Deck can be build or consist only by them if that's what you want. As long as it has 6 to 30 cards.

2) There are no hindrance cards or stages/events that allow Card Removal. It would be pointless as in ER [b]you can remove any card from your Deck any time you wish.[/b] Skill Cards can be re-added later, whereas the unique Class/Race Actions you find in Grimoires and Merchants are permanently lost, till you stumble on them again.

3) Item Cards like Potions and other consumables exist as cards in ER, they are placed in your Deck and you have to draw them to use them. Most of them have a limited time of uses. You can find them in Chests & buy them from Merchants. If they no longer suit your strategy you can remove them any time.

[i][b]Note:[/b] When you remove a Card from your Deck is removed from your Drawpile not from your Hand. And when you Add a Card in your Deck is added to your Drawpile next time you shuffle it. ie because you run out of cards.[/i]

4) There is a special type of Card [Equipment] representing your Main and Offhand Weapon/Item or Shield. These go to your inventory and as long as one of them is equipped you always draw it, and can use it once per turn. They don't count towards your Deck size, but they do take up one (or two) card slots from the cards you can draw each turn. You can find them in Chests & buy them from Merchants.

5) There isn't a stage for upgrading your cards. All instances of a card gain +1 XP each time they are used. Then once they gather the necessary XP their XP become 0, and [b]the cards upgrade automatically to their improved version[/b] as you use them. [i]Tier 0 cards, can't be upgraded, Tier 1 cards need 10 XP to upgrade once, Tier 2 cards need 10 XP to upgrade once, and another 20 to upgrade once more etc.[/i]

6) [b]You can't choose which dungeon branch to go next.[/b] Fight the Elite? Or Open the Chest? Sorry you have to fight that Elite even with your dying breath. Dungeons have a procedurally generated status-quo.

7) You can summon creatures to either fight your enemies or guard you.

8) There are 11 Types of Damage and Resistance (Slashing, Bludgeoning, Piercing, Fire, Air, Earth, Water, Light, Dark, Astral & Poison) Enemies may be strong vs some elements and weak vs others, so some times you'll have to be able to adapt your Deck on the fly, as you fight a certain enemy or boss. [b]The one deck to rule them all doesn't exist, if you get my drift...[/b]

9) A typical run consists of 7 Stages (instead of 3 or 4 I think?). Each Stage can have 8 to 18 nodes you have to clear and also defeat the Stage boss in order to proceed. [i]There is a way to prolong farming a Stage indefinitely.[/i]
So a single run can last from a few minutes to as long as you can survive.

You get Tokens & Mastery by clearing a Stage & defeating its Boss, and bonus Tokens & Mastery from your Final Score & Level reached.

10) There is 1/4 Races & 4/8 Classes already unlocked for you to play. Progressing through the game & defeating bosses give you Tokens, you can then choose which other Races & Classes you want to unlock.

11) Playing with a Race & Class, gives you Mastery in both the Race & Class, and with that new Skill Cards become available to use in your deck once you meet the level requirements.

12) Level Up: Leveling Up refills part of your Health & Action Points, it also increases one of your three dominant Attributes (Strength,Resilience,Agility,Intellect,Willpower or Charisma) by +1. (Which in turn affects all the stats these attributes govern).

13) You can play with any Race/Class combo you desire, but whether this combo actually works or not is up to you to find out. i.e I don't forbid you to play a Demon Exorcist, but be warned that your Light Aspect will be awfully weak.

14) Progress isn't saved when you quit, but on Entries, Camps & Intersections (see more info below)

15) You can't magically foresee what special move your enemy is planning to do.  You only realize it after the fact. Any special reaction other than attack, ie Heal, use Poison, Rage, use Concealment etc depend on their health levels and their Race & Class combination, so sooner or later it will make sense to you and after a few stages you'll be able to predict their attack & defense patterns and adapt your strategy accordingly. 

[b]Ok. This concludes the main gameplay differences I can think. [/b]


[h1]Let's now see what nodes you can currently find in each Stage as of the latest build.[/h1]

[list]
[*] [b]Entry:[/b] The Stage entrance. One of the three places where your progress is saved.
[*] [b]Encounter: [/b]You fight 1 to 3 random normal Enemies of the same faction or racial type. Enemies have both Tiers & Levels that determine which stage they can appear and their power level compared to the player.
[*] [b]Elite Encounter:[/b] You fight 1 to 4 random elite Enemies of higher level than yours. In many cases they are quite deadly, unless the RNG comes to your favor. The only way to avoid them is to take an intersection before you reach them.
[*] [b]Camp:[/b] The second place where your progress is saved. You can use 1 Ration to restore 10 AP & 10 HP one time per Camp.
[*] [b]Questionmark:[/b] Random Events, Discoveries & Opportunities. (Currently mostly Opportunities to loot Equipment & Farthings or learn new Actions.) Some of the choices will immediately exclude the others. In Example you can't both claim the Backpack contents and also the Grimoire Actions. You have to pick one, without knowing beforehand its contents.
[*] [b]Merchant:[/b] The wandering Merchant can sell you up to three random Equipment or Consumable Cards, including cards with the Unique descriptor.
[*] [b]Intersection:[/b] A hidden path. Each time you choose to follow it, you go to a (new) hidden area within the same stage, indefinitely prolonging your stay in the stage. For example if you wish to farm more XP, Farthings, Cards, Equipment or whatever before facing the stage boss. Taking an Intersection will lead you to a new Entry, where your progress is saved.
[*] [b]Town:[/b] There are three Towns. In stage 3, 5 & 7.  You can Rest, Buy Rations or Action Cards, Equipment & Consumables. The difference with the wandering Merchant is that the selection consists of 8 items (instead of 3), and you can either way keep refreshing the lists till you are satisfied that you got the best Cards your Mastery & Farthings can buy. 
[*] [b]Boss[/b]: A single usually very powerful enemy. You have to somehow defeat them in order to get the precious Tokens & Mastery and advance into the next stage.
[/list]


That's all for now folks. I'll be happy to answer any questions you may have!

notes.title: Initial Modding Support
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34785691/502081d99341c0dea95594dc020bc70fdee1b92e.jpg[/img]

Did you ever felt this burning desire to change something in a game, anything, but either it was impossible due to lack of modding support or way too complicated, because it required knowing a programming language you never used or ever cared to learn? 

I certainly have, too many times. So while the out of the box modding in Erannorth Reborn hasn't yet reached its heights of ease and accessibility, I think its already pretty straightforward. You can mod and change all major aspects of the game simply[u] by editing plain text files and copying files into specific folders.[/u]

Hopefully you won't feel the urge to change (many) things right away, but add new stuff instead.

So. Let's say you want to add a new card? All you need to think is what you need this card to do. [i]Hmm. I want a card that Deals 4 Ice (Water) Damage, every round for 3 rounds, and also cause the enemy to Bleed upon impact. Oh and also to Draw a Card and eventually restore all the actions I spend to cast this spell. Can I?[/i]

Yes actually you can. Open the proper text file, and add these two lines of text:
[i]Ice Barrage, Mystic
Echo:3, Damage:4, Bleed:1, Focus:1, Meditate:2, Actions:6, Tier:3, Element:Water[/i]

Echo, makes the Spell lasts 3 rounds, Damage to deal Damage, Bleed to cause bleeding, Focus to Draw a card, and Meditate to restore 2 AP each time the spell activates, Costs 6 Actions and deals Water damage (Water Element).

[b]Easy right? [/b]

Since you can already find the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1703719938]official modding guide[/url] in the Community Hub, I'll just mention briefly some of the modding possibilities: 

[list]
[*] Add custom artworks for your character.
[*] Edit every race, class, enemy and action card in the game.
[*] Change the Skill Trees.
[*] Edit the unlock costs of each race & class.
[*] Remove the unlock costs of each race & class completely.
[*] Remove every race, class, enemy and action card in the game. [i]Wait what?[/i]
[*] Add your own races, classes, enemies and action cards using in-game resources or your custom artworks.
[*] Change the current artworks of cards & enemies with your own.
[*] Do a total conversion mod to your favorite franchise. [i]It will hurt, but you can.[/i]
[/list]


[b]So yes, you can pretty much edit, add and remove everything that matters, 
without the need of any programming skills or knowledge.[/b]

Now probably the burning question you have consists of two words: [i]Steam Workshop?[/i]

Sort answer is not yet. While I do want you to go nuts with mods, many mods floating around in such an accessible manner, will make the balancing and bug-fixing efforts harder at this stage of development. 

I do hope to complete the Workshop integration during the final stages of the early access, but for now it has a very low priority in the Roadmap, and there are certain other things that need to arrive first.

In the meantime you can use the Nexus, and share your creations with the community for all of us to enjoy!

notes.title: The Races and Classes of Erannorth
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34785691/502081d99341c0dea95594dc020bc70fdee1b92e.jpg[/img]

In Erannorth Reborn, you take on the role of a Supernatural, so even as Human, you eventually unlock and possess Supernatural abilities like Telekinetic Powers, Sensing Thoughts, Reading Auras etc. And as a Vampire, Demon or Lycanthrope you possess a much higher level and array of powers. These innate powers you have can be combined with your Class expertise to create truly unique character builds and gameplay experiences. 

Lore wise, once the Story Mode is developed you'll get a better sense of what's going on in the World, and how does this involves you and you fit in the grand scheme of things. Running from an Order of Light might make sense, but who are those Resurgant Tenebris folk and why they too hunt you down? Aren't all Supernaturals a happy big family? Ehm, not quite... But let's leave this discussion for a later date.

In the meantime, and during the first stage of Early Access, the main and only game mode is the Gaunlet. Our main concearn is surviving as many stages as possible and collect the precious tokens and mastery to unlock new races, classes and action cards. You start out as a Human. Either Mercenary, Shadow, Mystic or Hunter and then you can unlock any Race or Class you prefer to play next. Unlocking new Races costs 60 Tokens, and Classes 30 Tokens. Tokens are traded to Unlock the Race/Class, whereas the Mastery unlocks stuff automatically as it increases.

[h1]Races[/h1]

[b]Human[/b]

Humans have no attribute adjustments (all attributes start at 10, AP at +3), no special bonuses or weaknesses and the potential to develop psychic and psionic powers. Human Skills include Read Aura, Telekinetic Bind, Second Sight etc.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34785691/826121b3210c2cfb6fc16fa68e17f02c8a783f09.jpg[/img]

[b]Vampire[/b]

Vampires have increased proficiency with actions that deal Dark Damage (+2), and major penalty (-3) in Actions that deal Fire & Light Damage. They also have vulnerability in Fire & Light (-2) Damage. Additionally they receive +4 HP, +6 AP, +2 Strength, +3 Agility, +1 Resilience, +2 Intellect, -3 Willpower & +1 Charisma. Vampire Skills include Feed, Nocturnal Claws, Hypnotic Gaze, Alacrity etc.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34785691/9e7b384a91c591b94d0cbcedb9087a792aa05858.jpg[/img]

[b]Demon[/b]

Demons have increased proficiency with actions that deal Astral & Fire Damage +2, but they are virtually unable to use Actions that deal Light Damage (-6). They have vulnerability in Water & Earth (-1) & Light (-2) Damage. Additionally they receive +5 HP, +5 AP, +1 Strength, +1 Agility, -1 Resilience, +2 Intellect, -1 Willpower & +3 Charisma. Demon Skills include Induce Sleep, Malediction, Infernal Servant, Possess etc.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34785691/a0775d2467f911347db19d4438314eda43069257.jpg[/img]

[b]Lycanthrope[/b]

Lycanthropes have increased proficiency with actions that deal Earth Damage (+2), and a major penalty (-3) in Actions that deal Fire & Dark Damage. They also have vulnerability in Fire & Dark (-2) Damage. Additionally they receive +6 HP, +4 AP, +4 Strength, +3 Agility, +3 Resilience, -1 Intellect, -2 Willpower & -2 Charisma. Lycanthrope Skills include Claw Strike, Hybrid Form, Regenerate, Rend etc.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34785691/c8ad4eba6b8362b7e7b7c70ccb95b662e2d3262c.jpg[/img]

[h1]Classes[/h1]

[b]Mercenary[/b]

A disciplined fighter, reckless barbarian and anything inbetween. In all cases though a true master of arms and warfare. Equipment of choice includes Swords, Axes and Shields. In addition to their racial stats Mercenaries receive +7 HP, +2 AP, +3 Strength, +1 Agility, +2 Resilience, -1 Intellect, -2 Willpower & +0 Charisma. Mercenary Skills include Quick Slash, Intimidate, Adrenaline Surge, Shield Bash etc, and they Specialize in Slashing & Bludgeoning Damage.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34785691/88c7930a4b8ab695a833276b52f0cbfeaed7b7c9.jpg[/img]

[b]Hunter[/b]

A relentless hunter of monsters and sometimes even of those of his/her own kind. Equipment of choice includes Silver Swords, Crossbows & Flintlock Pistols. In addition to their racial stats Hunters receive +6 HP, +3 AP, +1 Strength, Agility +3, Resilience +2, Intellect -1, Willpower +0, -2 Charisma. Hunter Skills include Camouflage, Net Trap, Multi Shot, Bolt (Silver) etc, and even though they Specialize in Slashing & Piercing Damage, their equipment can be enhanced to better deal with monsters of all types.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34785691/7a5ede280be380ae49fd51c54e06afbdbc2e90e0.jpg[/img]

[b]Shadow[/b]

More than a mere rogue or assassin, Shadows can tap into the mystical forces of darkness and manipulate the shadows to their advantage. Equipment of choice includes Daggers, Bladed Gaunlets & Poison. In addition to their racial stats Shadows receive +5 HP, +4 AP, +0 Strength, +3 Agility, -1 Resilience, +2 Intellect, -1 Willpower, +1 Charisma. Shadow Skills include Backstab, Shadow Step, Sneak Attack, Meld in Shadows etc, and they Specialize in Piercing, Dark & Poison Damage.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34785691/3cca1c9d8f0dd8e502e150c4422ec22d382c6aa2.jpg[/img]

[b]Mystic[/b]

A master of Fire, Air & Water, yet somehow totally unable to harness the power of Earth. Equipment of choice includes Staves, Wands & Spellbooks. In addition to their racial stats Mystics receive +2 HP, +7 AP, -2 Strength, +1 Agility, -1 Resilience, +3 Intellect, +2 Willpower, +0 Charisma. Mystic Skills include Firebolt, Blizzard, Gust of Wind, Stillness etc, and they Specialize in Fire, Water & Air Damage.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34785691/1f462eb4b7db2e69c7b0978b30661ded62c98581.jpg[/img]

[b]Animist[/b]

Animists can manipulate Earth, the soil & its plants. They have a natural affinity with Animals, and some can even assume their form. Equipment of choice includes Staves. In addition to their racial stats Animists receive +7 HP, +2 AP, +0 Strength, -2 Agility, +2 Resilience, +1 Intellect, +3 Willpower & -1 Charisma. Animist Skills include Herbal Infusion, Animate Vines, Harden Staff, Call Animal Ally etc, and they Specialize in Earth & Bludgeoning Damage.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34785691/c7bfaa5ffd40238c573e1f5c9e020fc10752cb6e.jpg[/img]

[b]Exorcist[/b]

Exorcists can see, summon and banish spirits. Somewhere in-between good evil, Exorcists can tap both into the powers of light & darkness. Equipment of choice includes Staves & Swords. In addition to their racial stats Exorcists receive +4 HP, +5 AP, +1 Strength, -2 Agility, -1 Resilience, +0 Intellect, +3 Willpower & +2 Charisma. Exorcist Skills include Prayer, Mend Wounds, Bloodpact, Call Spirit, Release Spirit etc, and they Specialize in both Light & Dark Damage.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34785691/565a7665eff93d8d0691c43a65f9318712c9c34b.jpg[/img]

[b]Necromancer[/b]

Necromancers can control the forces of death and darkness. Equipment of choice includes Staves & Scythes. In addition to their racial stats Necromancers receive +3 HP, +6 AP, -1 Strength, -2 Agility, +2 Resilience, +1 Intellect, +3 Willpower, +1 Charisma. Necromancer Skills include Chill Touch, Affliction, Reanimate, Plague, Curse etc, and they Specialize in Dark Damage.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34785691/11da7c37a47f3aaa822d42d06d81cbf6cdc214b5.jpg[/img]

[b]Witch[/b]

Beautiful, ageless (or at least they can always appear so) and deadly. Especially when relieved the burden of all garments. Equipment of choice is their Athame which allows them to harness the Astral energy. In addition to their racial stats Witches receive +1 HP, +8 AP, -1 Strength, -2 Resilience, +2 Intellect, +0 Willpower & +3 Charisma. Witch Skills include Distract, Jinx, Moondance, Seduce, Skyclad etc, and they Specialize in Astral & Piercing Damage.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34785691/e67efc521f14d6a8348c91e3db7d12d54d1f6974.jpg[/img]

So that's certainly a lot to take in, but everything will make more sense once you start actually playing with them. 

In the meantime if you have any questions, feel free to drop by the discussion board. Would be happy to answer them.

Till next time!

notes.title: Gameplay Basics and Deckbuilding 101
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34785691/502081d99341c0dea95594dc020bc70fdee1b92e.jpg[/img]

Erannorth Reborn is a Deck-building Roguelike-like, (or Rogue-lite if you prefer) RPG, and as such, it has all the things you expect. But most likely, not in the way you are used to have them.
 
[b]Do I need to build a deck to fight enemies with it? [/b]

[i]Absolutely.[/i] But constructing your deck is not entirely a matter of chance: You have access to a large pool of cards you can add and remove from your deck at any time. Your cards Upgrade by using them, and you can remove any Card from your deck anytime as long as you have at least 6 cards in it. [i](More on this shortly.)[/i]

[b]What about grinding and perma-death?[/b]

[i]Wouldn't be a rogue-lite without them![/i] But as long as you clear a stage you are [b]immediately[/b] rewarded with Tokens & Class/Race Mastery. Then each stage you clear yields additional Tokens & Mastery. No 0-yield runs when you deserve to earn something.

During the first month of Early Access the only game mode will be a Gaunlet, which at the moment of this writing, consists of 7 stages that progressively increase in length and difficulty. Each stage contains encounters, treasure, grimoires, campsite etc. [i]You can't, and you won't ever be able to choose whether to fight the elite encounter or instead to pick a tome for example. Each stage has a (procedurally generated) status quo. So no running from that Elite encounter. Sorry.[/i]

At the end of each stage you face a powerful boss. Defeating the 1st stage boss awards +1 Token & +1 Mastery, the 2nd +2 Tokens & +2 Mastery etc. So if you die on the 3rd stage your Run translates into +3 Tokens and +3 Mastery in your chosen Class & Race. Completing the 7th Stage not only gives the +7 Tokens & Mastery you expect, but also a +10 Completion bonus. Tokens are used to Unlock new Races & Classes, while Mastery higher Tier Action Cards.

[b]Attributes, Leveling & Character customization? [/b]

[i]Yes, yes & yes.[/i] It always buffled me why in Rogue-likes the Characters had to look in a particular fixed way? You want to play a Necromancer? It's a him, and that's his artwork. You want to play a Fighter? It's a her and that's her artwork. While of course I cannot predict or provide artworks for every taste, I tried to give you a varied choice of looks to build your character, as well as the ability to use a custom one. So while creating your character you pick your gender and looks, your race & class. These info along with your character's name are automatically saved, so in the next run, you don't have to do any customizing unless you want to. Additionally you have two preset slot, for quickly saving/loading alternative characters.

[b]Ok so I created my character, now what?[/b]

In your first run you don't have many choices or power. You are just a Human Mercenary: a mere mortal with lots of unrealized potential.

Your Race & Class combination will determine your Starting Attributes, which have effect in your proficiency dealing certain types of Damage. i.e A Demon Exorcist is possible but will surely suck if you go for the "Light" side of things, on the other hand it will be extremely challenging to attempt it. So whatever makes you happy. It will also determine your Starting Cards pool and the Skill Cards you have access: 6 Racial  & 18 Class Skill Cards.

[h1]Deckbuilding[/h1]

Your Deck needs to have at least 6 Cards, that can be any of the following cards:

[b]Skill Cards from your Race & Class[/b]

These are Cards that you unlock permanently by increasing your Class & Race Masteries. So at Mastery 0, you have access to Tier 1 Cards, at 15 you have access to Tier 2 Cards etc. The highest your Race or Class Mastery the more options you get. Skill Cards are truly invaluable in the Deckbuilding process.
Once unlocked: a)If you meet their level requirements you can add/remove them [b]freely[/b] from your Deck. b) You may find them in Grimoires & use them even if you don't meet their level requirements. You can build your deck entirely with Skill Cards, or use them selectively as the situation demands. But keep in mind that when adding new Skills you add them to your Discard pile, not your Draw Pile, and when you remove them you remove them from Both (Discard & Draw Pile), but not from your Hand.

[b]Grimoire Cards either Generic or Specific to your Race & Class[/b]

These are Cards that you find randomly in forgotten Grimoires. They can be either Skill Cards you have unlocked (whether you meet the level requirements or not). Or Rare Action Cards you have unlocked by achieving higher Masteries. In Example if you have reached Mastery 15, in Mercenary you can potentially find up to Tier 2 Mercenary Cards. These special Grimoire cards can only be found in Tomes, and you can have up to 3 copies in your Deck. You can remove them any time from your Deck but once you do they are lost forever, or till you stumble upon them in another tome.

[b]Equipment Cards either Generic or Specific to your Race & Class[/b]

Equipment are Cards, you can either find in Chests, as random drops or in Merchants. Your character at any time has a Main Weapon equipped, and then you can optionally equip an Offhand Weapon, Item or Shield. Equipment eat up space in your Hand, but you can consistently use it once per turn. So at the very least, each turn you can rely on your Weapon to attack enemies.
Additionally you can switch to any Equipment you own in your Inventory at any moment, if you meet the level requirements. Fighting a Skeleton and your Bow is useless? Switch to your Mace, and next turn start attacking with it instead! Suspect a tough fight ahead? Bring in your Shield etc. Equipment can make your strategies more consistent and also help you adapt in seemingly dire situations, its also harmless to your current tactics to pick them up, as they just go straight into your inventory and not in your deck.

[b]Consumable Cards either Generic or Specific to your Race & Class[/b]

These are Cards with limited uses, i.e if a Consumable has 3 uses, if you use it 3 times then its automatically removed from your Deck. You can find them in Chests, in Merchants or as Random Drops. You can have up to 3 copies in your Deck and you can remove them any time from it. But once you do, they are lost till you acquire them again. To use a consumable you have to draw it first. 

So as you can see your Deck strategy can be consistent by relying to your Race & Class Skill Cards, and still get unique and enriched by the occasional rare Actions you find in Grimoires, Equipment & Consumables you find in Merchants & Chests and more. The Mastery you acquire, will make future runs easier as it will give you more tools and options for Deckbuilding and more powerful cards. Your race also matters. A Human Mystic, a Vampire Mystic, a Demon Mystic & Lycanthrope Mystic, while all have access to Mystic Actions; are different in more ways than you think, each with unique strategies, strengths & weaknesses you have to account for if you hope to beat the Gaunlet.

If you have any questions, feel free to drop by the discussion board. Would be happy to answer them.

Till next time!

notes.title: Development Roadmap and Plans for the Early Access
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/34785691/502081d99341c0dea95594dc020bc70fdee1b92e.jpg[/img]

Hello everyone,

With the EA release coming soon, I think it's a good time, that you all know my plans for the Early Access and my overall philosophy of what this development phase means to me, so there won't be any miscommunications or disappointments and make an informed decision whether to get involved in it, or not.

For me the EA phase is where the true development of Erannorth Reborn [b]begins[/b], as now, we (you and I), can actually work together and build something beautiful. I am a firm believer that what makes a game truly great is its community; and my focus so far has been to provide a complete and easy framework, that will allow modders and creative players to create and add their own content to the game. To really get involved; and do so easily with ZERO coding experience, by editing plain text files. I already added a guide covering modding basics in the Community page so make sure to check it out!

I am also a firm believer that when developers do waterfall development, completely disregarding their audience, 90% of the cases is an unmitigated disaster! 

So aside for overall polishing, Bugfixes, Typo/Grammar Corrections (I'll really need your help with that: English isn't my native language) and acting on (or at least considering) your own feedback on both planned & unplanned features, this is what I have in mind of doing during EA:

[h1]Erannorth Reborn EA Roadmap[/h1]

[h1]Game Balance & Difficulty[/h1]

[i]Top Priority[/i]
[list]
[*] Adjust Difficulty to what most of the game community considers as 'Normal' Difficulty. 
[*] Balance the Actions, Enemies & Enemies' abilities accordingly.
[/list]

[h1]New Content[/h1]

[i] High Priority [/i]
[list]
[*] New Enemy AI Behaviors & Enemies
[*] New Action Effects & Actions
[*] Random Events to Spice up the Gaunlet
[*] Improved Tutorial (categorized in sections) covering more (and advanced) Game concepts (Based on your feedback)
[/list]

[h1]New Features[/h1]

[i]High Priority[/i]
[list]
[*] Add Difficulty setting to let users decide between Easy, Normal & Hard modes, and the overall amount of Gaunlet Stages (before completing their run).
[*] Quality of Life Improvements based on your feedback
[*] Story Mode
[/list]

[i]Medium Priority[/i]
[list]
[*] User Leaderboards with Best Completion Time, Runs etc. for the Gaunlet
[*] Personal Records, Best Completion Times, Runs etc. for the Gaunlet
[/list]

[h1]Graphics & Visuals[/h1]
[i]High Priority[/i]
[list]
[*] Extra PC Characters, Outfits and other Cosmetics based on your feedback
[/list]

[h1]Modding Support[/h1]

[i]High Priority[/i]
[list]
[*]Quality of Modding Improvements based on your feedback
[/list]

[i]Medium Priority[/i]
[list]
[*]Users & modders can edit & override the Localization file
[*]Mods are self-contained in their own folders
[*]User-friendly in-game Manager or Utility to Install/Uninstall Mods (from .ZIP files)
[/list]

[i]Low Priority - If everything else is done [/i]
[list]
[*]Steam Workshop support (Requires me to first complete the Medium Priority items)
[*]Users & Modders can edit/create & add new Stories for the Story Mode
[/list]

Once everything in this list is done hopefully within the next 3 to 6 months, Erannorth Reborn will be ready for wide Release. Will this be the end? Hopefully not, but just another beginning. If all go well, I will keep supporting the game and the community, with additional content, dlc & expansions.

But while dreaming the future is always a good thing, talking about it not necessarily so. :lunar2019grinningpig:

That's all I wanted to say for now. Looking forward to see you in the Discussion board!
